home.title: The only framework you can pick at any point.
home.subtitle: Day 1 or day 400: your routes, your pages, your rendering and your data stay put. What you rewrite is the model — one entity at a time.
home.gradientText: A Frond runs in-process or in its own process behind JSON-RPC 2.0 — with identical user code. No RPC without travel: local calls are direct memory execution.
home.statAxesText: one field states its shape, role, lifecycle and boundary — every projection reads from them
home.statPrimitivesText: the whole call surface: useQuery, useCommand, useFormFor and useCurrentUser in the page, and invoke, their server dual
home.dogfoodTitle: This site is a Fougere app
home.dogfoodText: The docs you are about to read are markdown in git. The blog behind /blog is a Frond: posts are entities with a judged draft→publish transition, written through the form contract, read through the query primitive — and the whole Frond can move to another process by uncommenting one line of config.
home.realCode: The code below is this site's own blog Frond — not pseudocode.
home.declareText: One entity class. Validation, SQLite table, GraphQL type, form contract — all projections of it.
home.judgeText: Operations, not field writes. readOnly closes the inbound door; the server stamps the pair.
home.consumeText: The imported class designates the call. A command on Post revalidates every query on Post.
home.gradientPoint1: Errors travel intact: same code, message and per-field details either side
home.gradientPoint2: Session state reaches remote collectors — trust is intra-topology
home.gradientPoint3: Dead host → typed 503 in your pages; restart → recovery, app untouched
home.foreignTitle: A Frond does not have to be TypeScript
home.foreignText: A Frond honours two contracts and both are JSON: the wire (JSON-RPC 2.0) and the map (rpc.discover, which returns what it hosts, schemas included). Neither mentions TypeScript. demos/rust-frond is a telemetry domain written in Rust — there is no entity class anywhere in it, the declaration lives in src/main.rs.
home.foreignAxes: The consumer asks for the map, rebuilds a live schema from it, and refuses a bad payload before any network happens. Those refusals are the four axes crossing a language boundary: shape is the JSON Schema, role, lifecycle and boundary ride under x-fougere. The rules travel, not just the types.
home.foreignCaption: Rules declared in Rust, enforced by the TypeScript judge — no line of TS declared them
home.derivationTitle: The model: one declaration, everything projects
home.derivationText: An entity is not a table. The table, the validation, the form, the API are projections of one declaration — change it, every projection follows.
home.compareText: A consequence you can see: without a model, every app re-declares the same shape in the validator, the table, the endpoint and the form — four files that must never drift. With one, the declaration is alone and everything else derives.
home.compareBeforeLabel: 4 declarations of the same shape, kept in sync by hand
home.auditTitle: Don't take our word — make your agent count
home.auditText: The duplicated glue is the measurable trace of a missing model. Paste this prompt into the AI agent that already knows your codebase (Claude Code, Cursor…): it counts the re-declared shapes and the sync wiring in your app — and reports the adoption costs just as carefully.
home.statusText: Pre-release — but not a promise. Each of these has been seen running:
home.status1: The 5 primitives are the only path — the old world was deleted, not half-replaced
home.status2: A judged business feature (draft→publish) verified in the browser, badge flip included
home.status3: The split is lived daily: kill the host → typed 503 in the pages; restart → recovery
home.status4: Identical user code in-process and split — verified down to the production build
home.status5: This site — docs, blog, auth — runs on it
home.oneIdeaTitle: One idea, and it is the kind you can check
home.oneIdeaText: The declaration names nothing outside itself — no table, no protocol, no host, no address. So what it does not name is either derived from it, or chosen outside it. The two sections below are those two readings, and nothing else.
